newsitem.title: CHINA: China commission approves $400m JV with UK's ICI.
newsitem.headline: China commission approves $400m JV with UK's ICI.

text.p: China's State Planning Commission has approved a $400 million joint venture between Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc and Shanghai Tianyuan Chemical Works, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The chemical venture, the largest of its kind in Shanghai, would be located in the city's new petrochemical development base along northern Hangzhou Bay, the newspaper, published by the official China Daily, said.
The factory was designed to produce raw materials used in making polyurethane, which is used in the auto, household appliance and building industries.
The plant would have an annual production capacity of 75,000 to 120,000 tonnes of anline, and 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes of nitrobenzene, it said, adding both were industrial chemicals.
The venture was now awaiting final approval from the State Council, or cabinet, it said, but gave no further details.
The State Planning Commission had reviewed the proposal because investment exceeded $30 million, it said.
